title: The Leeward Compass
premise: Mirabel Nystrom, a riverboat captain who has spent a decade dodging debts and authorities on the Vellwater, is hired by a desperate widow to find her husband, a surveyor whose government team vanished near the river's forbidden headwaters. The only clue is the man's brass compass, which points not north but toward something buried beneath the glacier — a pre-collapse survey vault holding land claims that could free an entire valley of indentured families, including Mirabel's own inherited debt. Racing the calving season that will seal the route for another year, Mirabel is pursued by the Survey's enforcer, who wants the vault destroyed and its witnesses with it. At the source, Mirabel must choose between selling the compass to buy his own freedom or opening the vault for everyone; he opens it, loses his boat in the calving flood, and returns downstream carrying not a debt but a claim — the first thing he has ever owned.
about_author: Z. M. Kavanagh spent seven years as a deckhand on inland freight routes before turning to writing, and still keeps a waterlogged chart of a river that no longer exists. Kavanagh writes adventure fiction about people whose livelihoods depend on reading landscapes that governments would prefer to erase.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He pilots a cargo run down the Vellwater, reading the river's shifting moods while quietly avoiding a port official who knows his face. A small scene of competence and isolation establishes his invisibility as survival. Emotional beat: weary contentment built on deliberate forgetting.

chapters.title: A Widow at Graylock Landing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Sela Voss finds him at a dockside tavern, offering double his usual rate to search for her husband Aldric, missing with a government survey team. She carries Aldric's brass compass, which trembles off true. Mirabel refuses twice, then sees the debt mark burned into her contract papers. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition of himself in her desperation.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Testing the compass aboard his boat, the Kestrel, he realizes it ignores magnetic north entirely, swinging instead toward the glacier fields upstream. His old river mentor's warnings about the forbidden headwaters surface in memory. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding hard-won caution.

chapters.title: The Survey's Shadow
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the market town of Corren's Ford, he learns the vanished team was mapping 'anomalies' in the upper valley — and that a Survey enforcer named Captain Dree Halloway has arrived asking after boats. Mirabel lies smoothly but notices his name already on a list. Emotional beat: the chill of being seen.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Calendar
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He takes Sela aboard and begins the ascent through the middle reaches, navigating rapids that grow harder daily as meltwater rises. Their uneasy partnership forms over shared labor. Flashback: how his father signed away their family claim and drowned owing it. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as fuel.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. They pass a village half-swallowed by a reservoir created by the Survey's dam works; survivors live in stilted ruins, indentured to the company that flooded them. An old woman recognizes the compass and calls it 'the key they couldn't break.' Emotional beat: horror at what inheritance means here.

chapters.title: Halloway Catches the Current
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Halloway's gunboat appears behind them, flying inspection colors. Mirabel hides the Kestrel in a side slough he alone knows, watching from reeds as Halloway interrogates villagers and leaves one beaten. Emotional beat: cold fury replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. To pass the Gorge Narrows he must bargain with Osket Brann, a smuggler queen who controls the portage. Brann offers to hide them — if Mirabel surrenders the compass. He refuses; Sela secretly negotiates passage using her wedding ring. Emotional beat: shame at what others pay for his pride.

chapters.title: Night on the Shingle
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Camped below the glacier's moraine, Sela tells Mirabel the truth: Aldric wasn't just surveying — he found evidence the Survey manufactured the valley's debts to seize ancestral lands, and hid proof in a vault at the source. The compass is his locator. Emotional beat: trust forged in confession.

chapters.title: The First Calving
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A distant glacier face calves with a sound like the world cracking; the route window is open but closing. They abandon the Kestrel and travel light up the ice-carved canyon. Mirabel grieves leaving his boat — his last possession. Emotional beat: loss as liberation.

chapters.title: Tracks That End Nowhere
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They find the vanished survey camp: gear intact, meals half-eaten, no bodies. A survivor's journal describes the compass 'singing' near the ice wall before the team walked into the whiteout together. Emotional beat: dread that the mountain itself conspires.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm traps them in a crevasse field for two days; Mirabel navigates by memory and the trembling compass while Sela succumbs to frostbite fear. They find shelter in an ice cave where the walls hold ancient carved marks — older than any government. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared peril.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The compass pulls them to a fissure behind the calving face: inside, a natural cavern holds Aldric's hidden cache — documents, ledgers, and a recording cylinder naming every fabricated debt. But Aldric's frozen body sits beside it, having stayed to guard the proof. Emotional beat: awe curdling into sorrow.

chapters.title: Halloway at the Source
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Halloway arrives with two men, having tracked them since the gorge. She offers Mirabel a captain's commission and full debt forgiveness to hand over the documents and let the glacier take the rest. She reveals she grew up in the drowned village. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Price of Invisible Men
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel stalls, asking Halloway why she serves those who erased her home. Her answer — that power is the only shelter — cracks something in him. He pretends to accept, buying time as the glacier groans toward its great calving. Emotional beat: understanding his enemy without forgiving her.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Blue Ice
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. One of Halloway's men turns on her, ordered by superiors to leave no witnesses at all. In the chaos, Sela seizes the document satchel; Mirabel uses his knowledge of the ice to collapse the route behind them, trapping Halloway's surviving man. Halloway herself falls into the widening fissure reaching for the satchel. Emotional beat: victory that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The Glacier Opens
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The great calving begins — the entire face releases, and the melt-flood roars down the canyon toward the valley. Mirabel and Sela climb for high ground, watching the route close forever behind them and the flood carry away everything the Survey built below. Emotional beat: terrible, necessary destruction.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They walk down through the changed valley, past the breached dam and the freed reservoir waters finding their old channels. Villagers emerge from the stilted ruins, reading the flood as judgment. Mirabel carries the satchel against his chest like a second heartbeat. Emotional beat: exhausted pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Reading the Proof Aloud
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. At Corren's Ford, the documents are read publicly at the market cross; the fabricated debt rolls are read name by name, including Nystrom. Old debts are voided; the valley's families hold their own land for the first time in three generations. Emotional beat: catharsis, and disbelief that it worked.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Owns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Legally freed, Mirabel is offered command of the rebuilt river trade — respectability at last. He almost refuses out of habit, then signs, realizing he is choosing rather than escaping. He visits his father's grave with the voided debt paper. Emotional beat: quiet astonishment at belonging.

chapters.title: The Compass Rests
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The brass compass, its work done, finally settles to true north. Mirabel mounts it in the wheelhouse of a new boat he names for Sela's husband. Some nights he swears it still trembles toward the mountains, keeping faith with what the ice now guards. Emotional beat: peace without forgetting.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, coda. A year later, Mirabel pilots passengers up the reopened middle river, teaching a young deckhand to read sandbars. When the boy asks what's beyond the gorge, Mirabel says: 'Something worth the walk.' The river runs clear where the dam stood. Emotional beat: inheritance passed forward, freely given.
